B. Is this measure already running in Kymenlaakso wellbeing services county (or in the HUS university hospital area that treats its patients)?
A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure raise the share of lung cancer patients who get curative-intent treatment, and by how much?
Measure: Fitness assessment and prehabilitation before deciding against curative treatment. Before a stage I-III patient is judged too frail, they get an exercise test, a geriatric assessment if over 75, and four weeks of supervised exercise, breathing training and help to stop smoking. Then the decision is made again.
supported_en: Cochrane 2022: exercise training before lung surgery more than halves postoperative lung complications (RR 0.45).
not_supported_en: No page shows that prehabilitation raises the share of patients treated with curative intent, so the assumed 0.5 percentage points is untested.
summary_en: B: HUS's lung cancer pathway page says surgery is the first choice unless physical condition, other illnesses or lung function prevent it, but it describes no prehabilitation or second fitness review before that decision. Kymenlaakso's Leiko unit only handles general assessment and pre-surgery tests for planned operations. A: A 2022 Cochrane review (10 RCTs) found that exercise before lung surgery cuts lung complications after it (RR 0.45), but it did not measure how many more patients became fit for curative treatment.
unanswered_en: Two extra searches found no HUS or Kymenlaakso page about lung cancer prehabilitation, geriatric assessment or a second review of fitness for surgery.
